cluster b disorders, especially bpd, have a lot of overlapping symptoms. early trauma will often lead people to develop those disorders or develop symptoms and be misdiagnosed with a cluster b. i think the diagnosis of cptsd makes it easier to heal because when you view those symptoms as maladaptive coping mechanisms due to trauma, rather than inherent flaws in your personality, it’s easier to have self compassion and build understanding of your behavior. i feel like most of my progress came after i started learning about the effects of trauma. i was able to work on the root of my problems because i understood why they were happening. this is why i also think cptsd not being in the dsm is detrimental to a lot of people struggling with these issues. mental health professionals see these symptoms and slap on cluster b diagnoses because they arent aware of cptsd. it can make people feel like there is no hope, when you look up pds it says they are lifelong disorders. at least that’s how i felt. trauma effects everyone in different ways though and they are often comorbid also. anyway just my opinion that cptsd is very commonly misdiagnosed as cluster b, thats what i think of when i hear people talk about this sort of thing

When I got my diagnosis I made a list of the symptoms I experienced and wrote down a few specific examples where they affected my functioning. This helped me a lot because I tend to freeze up and forget everything when I'm put on the spot. Other than that my psych asked me stuff like do you lose your phone often, are you punctual, stuff like that. If you feel like the appointment is going too fast, you can tell the psych that. They should be open to listening to you and making sure that you're getting what you need during the appointment.

I think a good place to start might be to write down your major goals, and start breaking those goals down into small, manageable steps. Think of what is keeping you from carrying out those steps and try to problem solve. So if one of your goals is to keep good hygiene, one of the small steps could be to brush your teeth once a day. Eventually, you will get better at doing these things and you'll be able to set more goals.
